home.headline: How does the interplay of neural architecture and dynamics give rise to intelligent function?
home.intro: I am an Assistant Professor in the School of Computer Science at Peking University. Viewing the brain as a complex dynamical computer, my lab works in NeuroAI at the intersection of computer science, neuroscience, physics, and mathematics to unravel the computational principles of the brain and develop brain-inspired and brain-like computing frameworks. Prior to joining PKU, I conducted postdoctoral research in computational neuroscience with Prof. Wolfgang Maass at Graz University of Technology and doctoral research in neurophysics with Prof. Pulin Gong at the University of Sydney.
home.research_intro: Centered on NeuroAI, our research investigates the bidirectional coupling of Architecture ↔ Dynamics ↔ Function: how cellular biophysics and circuit connectivity shape emergent spatiotemporal dynamics to realize cognitive and sensory function, and how distilling these coupled mechanisms yields data-efficient, noise-robust brain-inspired and brain-like intelligent systems.
home.embodied_ai: Extending Architecture ↔ Dynamics ↔ Function into physical interaction, we explore brain-inspired and brain-like embodied AI that couples microsecond spike perception, iterative recurrent state refinement, and continuous attractor dynamics for robotic manipulation, 3D vision, and autonomous systems.

research.headline: NeuroAI: Unraveling the Coupling of Neural Architecture, Dynamics, and Function
research.intro: Our lab approaches biological and artificial intelligence as a unified problem in NeuroAI. Rather than treating circuit anatomy, population dynamics, and behavioral function as separate topics, we investigate Architecture ↔ Dynamics ↔ Function as one coupled dynamical system across computer science, neuroscience, physics, and mathematics. Mechanistic models of cortical microcircuits guide the design of brain-inspired and brain-like intelligent architectures, while spectral, statistical-physical, and generative machine learning tools help decode how biological brains compute and learn.
research.relationship_title: The Core Coupling: Architecture ↔ Dynamics ↔ Function
research.relationship: Intelligent function emerges from the tight interaction among structural substrates, spatiotemporal dynamics, and task demands. At the architectural level, single-neuron ion-channel and dendritic nonlinearities, cellular heterogeneity, and non-random connectome motifs define a circuit's state space and structural inductive bias. These anatomical and physiological constraints sculpt rich non-equilibrium dynamics, including traveling waves, input-slaved transients, multiscale continuous attractors, iterative latent trajectories, and critical phase transitions. In turn, the spatiotemporal correlations embedded in those dynamics support functions where biological brains excel: sparse flexible coding, local credit assignment, rapid few-shot adaptation, out-of-distribution robustness, and low-latency sensorimotor control.

highlights.intro: Our research in NeuroAI is organized around three connected scientific questions that trace Architecture ↔ Dynamics ↔ Function from biophysical neurons and connectomes to scalable machine learning and embodied spike systems, supported by btorch, our open-source PyTorch ecosystem for simulating and training brain-inspired recurrent and spiking networks.

stories.title: How do biophysical neurons, cellular heterogeneity, and connectome rules shape spatiotemporal dynamics for cortical function?
stories.description: Cortical circuits are sparse, heterogeneous graphs built from strongly nonlinear neurons rather than uniform dense layers. Combining single-neuron kernel-spectral complexity analysis, data-constrained primary visual cortex models, generative connectome representations, and spatial spectral theory, we uncover how cellular nonlinearities, timescale diversity, and local excitation-inhibition motifs sculpt traveling waves, input-slaved transients, and flexible condition-dependent spike-order codes for noise-robust perception and working memory.

stories.title: How do non-equilibrium dynamics, criticality, and biological plasticity drive credit assignment and rapid adaptation?
stories.description: Biological networks compute and learn far from equilibrium without global backpropagation. We show how modulating ongoing critical waves accelerates active visual perception, how critical transition regimes generate superdiffusive attention spotlights and propagate global error information for strictly local online credit assignment, and how fractal loss superdiffusion, evolved heterogeneous plasticity, and invariant continuous attractors support rapid, few-shot adaptation.

stories.title: How can brain-inspired inductive biases, iterative dynamics, and spike representations power data-efficient AI and embodied systems?
stories.description: Translating neurophysical principles into machine learning yields architectures that generalize from limited data and compute efficiently in physical time. By embedding weight-reusing iterative latent dynamics, spectral state-space initializations, hippocampal multiscale spatial codes, scale-free and fixed-dimension attention structures, and adaptive recurrent spiking refinement into modern models, we advance value learning, high-resolution generation, microsecond stereo depth estimation, and point-cloud-free robotic grasping.
